Step 3 — Final Brief (the Task for AI)
Source guide: Client Intake & Briefing Toolkit (Pass 3 — Close). This is a hard stop — the cheapest gate in the engine,
preventing the most expensive failure.
 Purpose                      Reconcile everything gathered, fill or consciously park every gap, and lock a single approved brief — the
                              definitive task the AI engine will build the strategy from. No research starts until the brief and the
                              measurement brief are approved in writing.
 Frameworks & tools           The gap register (required field × have it? × source × owner × by when) covering: business problem/objective;
                              priority audiences & current state; reputation problem/desired perception; decision-maker & approval path;
                              baseline data & measurement access; constraints, guardrails & AI permissions; budget, timeline & markets. The
                              final-brief gate + the mandatory Measurement Brief (baseline, target, source, owner — see Step 10). Evidence-
                              readiness screen (below).
 What the AI drafts           Assembles the one-page Client Intake Brief from Steps 1–2; maintains the gap register and flags which required
                              fields are still empty; drafts the Measurement Brief skeleton.
 What the human owns          Confirms the problem is stated at reputation/company level — not as a tactic; confirms there are no material
                              unknowns; sets the engagement tier, governance and AI-status; secures written approval from the decision-
                              maker.
 Quality gate (HARD STOP)     The problem is at company/reputation level; no undisclosed risk remains; tier, governance and AI-status are
                              set; the brief AND the measurement brief are approved in writing by the decision-maker. No downstream work
                              begins otherwise.
 Deliverable                  Approved One-Page Client Intake Brief + Approved Measurement Brief
 Document format              Word/PDF: the one-page brief (Client & context; Organizational objective; Reputation problem/opportunity;
                              Priority audiences; Desired change; Stakeholders & alignment; Constraints & guardrails; Assets & access;
                              Success & measurement; Scope & logistics) + one-page Measurement Brief. Both PDF-locked with written
                              approval recorded. Google Drive.

Evidence readiness & gap check (from CD-S-002 · Phase 2)
1. Inventory known, verifiable facts (high-trust inputs).
2. List missing inputs that block a locked strategy.
3. Flag inconsistencies — do not resolve by assertion.
4. Separate fact vs. agency-proposal vs. situation/trigger.
5. Run compliance / MNPI / confidentiality screen GATE.
6. State strategic judgment: is input strong enough for a first build?
pages.p-0017:
Step 10 — Measurement & Evaluation
Source guide: Campaign Measurement Framework (AMEC-based). Start with the business change, then work backwards to
activities and metrics. Not advisory — adjudicated.
Purpose                    Demonstrate not just that a campaign was visible, but whether the intended audience noticed it, understood
                           it, acted differently, and contributed to a meaningful client outcome — the same way, whoever ran it.
Frameworks & tools         The AMEC chain (Organizational objectives → Communication objectives → Inputs → Activities → Outputs →
                           Outtakes → Outcomes → Impact) with the vertical rule. The Measurement Brief (approved at Step 3). The KPI
                           ladder (measures on ≥ 3 levels, incl. one outtake/outcome); Quality Coverage Rate (replaces clip counts);
                           engagement quality; disciplined SOV. KPI modules by campaign type (corporate reputation, employer
                           branding, crisis in scope). PESO measurement chain. Reporting cadence: baseline before launch; daily/weekly
                           during; one-page executive scorecard after. Attribution wording auto-matched to confidence (generated /
                           contributed to / coincided with).
What the AI drafts         Selects KPIs from the vetted set per campaign type; wires tagging/UTM/CRM fields; assembles daily/weekly
                           reports and the executive scorecard; matches attribution wording to the evidence confidence level; flags any
                           KPI without a baseline/target.
What the human owns        Approves the organizational objective and success criteria; establishes baseline, KPI definitions and
                           interpretation; turns weekly findings into execution decisions; judges attribution and alternative explanations.
Quality gate (three        Measurement gate: no brief approved without baseline, target, source, owner. Optimization gate: weekly
checkpoints)               performance must produce a documented decision. Learning gate: closure adds ≥ 3 findings to the benchmark
                           & learning library. Non-negotiables enforced: no AVEs; no impressions-as-reach; positive sentiment ≠ impact;
                           show baseline/target/result/trend together; distinguish what UP delivered vs what audiences did vs what
                           changed for the client.
Deliverable                Ongoing performance reports + the One-Page Executive Scorecard
Document format            Weekly headline-KPI report (5 KPIs vs target, action required) + a one-page scorecard (Objective/KPI × baseline
                           × target × result × status × insight × decision) followed by the eight-part evaluation narrative. Dashboard +
                           Word/PDF. Google Drive.

pages.p-0030:
Techniques to get more, and better
    ●     Research first. Every question should show you already know the brand, industry and market.
    ●     Open, then probe. Ask broad, then ladder down with “why?” and “so what?” until you reach the real
          answer, not the rehearsed one.
    ●     Talk to several people. One contact gives one truth; the C-suite gives the real, conflicting picture.
    ●     Ask for documents and data. Annual report, research, tracking, past campaigns, and analytics/CRM
          access — evidence beats opinion.
    ●     Listen for the unsaid. The tension, the hesitation, the misperception they downplay — that's often
          where the insight lives.
    ●     Reflect back. Play the problem back in your words before you leave — misunderstandings surface
          immediately.

The brief is not final until every required field is filled or consciously parked. Track it:

The final-brief gate (Step 3)
Before any strategy work begins, confirm:
    ●     The problem is stated at reputation / company level — not as a tactic (“we need a press release” is not a
          brief).
    ●     There are no material unknowns; any undisclosed risk has been surfaced and discussed.
    ●     The engagement tier, governance and AI-status are set.
    ●     The brief — and the measurement brief (baseline, target, source, owner) — are approved in writing by the
          decision-maker.
This is a hard stop. No research starts before the brief and the measurement brief are approved. It's the
cheapest gate in the whole engine and it prevents the most expensive failure — building a brilliant strategy for
the wrong problem.
pages.p-0080:
How this fits the engine
This is the definitive methodology for the CUBE's Measurement face and Step 13 of the guided flow. It replaces
the lighter measurement summary in the Master Blueprint (§13) and becomes the engine's measurement
standard.
Central rule: start with the business change, then work backwards to activities and metrics. Reach and coverage
remain useful diagnostics, but success is judged through audience response, behaviour change and
organizational impact.

Why it is operator-independent
    ●   The Measurement Brief is a hard gate. No campaign enters creative development without an approved
        brief (baseline, target, source, owner) — so a novice can't skip it.
    ●   The KPI ladder and campaign-type modules are fill-in templates. The operator selects the right KPIs
        from a vetted set rather than judging what to measure.
    ●   The non-negotiables are enforced rules. No AVEs, no impressions-as-reach,
        baseline+target+result+trend always shown — the system won't render a report that breaks them.
    ●   The attribution wording is auto-matched to the evidence. “Generated / contributed to / coincided
        with” is set by the confidence level, not the operator's optimism.
Enforced by the Review Board. The Adversarial Review Board's CFO persona attacks any KPI without a
baseline/target/benchmark, and the Journalist persona attacks any impact claim that outruns its evidence — so
this framework is not advisory, it is adjudicated.
pages.p-0082:
2. Mandatory measurement brief
No campaign enters creative development until the account lead and client approve this one-page brief.

Business definition
    ●     Business problem or opportunity · Organizational objective
    ●     Priority audiences and their current state · Desired audience change
    ●     Campaign period and relevant markets · Commercial, regulatory or reputational constraints

Objective formula
  Write every objective this way
  By [date], increase/decrease [audience change] among [specific audience] from [baseline] to [target],
  contributing to [organizational objective].
  Example: By 30 September, increase aided awareness of Brand X's sustainability commitment among urban
  consumers aged 25–44 from 28% to 38%, contributing to stronger brand preference.
Use no more than: one organizational objective · three communication objectives · five executive KPIs.

Measurement design — record for every KPI
Field                                   Field                                    Field
Definition & calculation                Baseline                                 Target
Data source                             Collection frequency                     Owner
Audience / market breakdown             Attribution method                       Known limitations
Targets should reflect the starting baseline, market maturity, available resources and the client's control over
execution. Multi-market campaigns combine a small number of global KPIs with locally appropriate targets.
pages.p-0087:
7. Attribution & evidence standards
Assign each impact claim a confidence level, and match the wording to it.
Confidence                 Evidence                                                                          Permitted wording
High                       Controlled experiment, matched markets, exposed-vs-unexposed research, or         “The campaign generated…”
                           strong CRM attribution
Medium                     Time-series change supported by multiple data sources and a credible              “The campaign contributed to…”
                           campaign linkage
Low                        Correlation or directional evidence without control for other factors             “The result coincided with the campaign
                                                                                                             and suggests…”

Guard against false causation. Never claim causation from media coverage, engagement or before-and-after
data alone. Record product changes, price promotions, competitor activity, seasonality and major news events as
possible alternative explanations.


8. Governance inside United Partners
Role                                           Accountability
Client lead                                    Approves organizational objective, business data and success criteria
Account director                               Owns the measurement brief and client alignment
Strategy / Insights lead                       Establishes baseline, KPI definitions, methodology and interpretation
Channel leads                                  Implement tagging, collect data and optimize activity
Analyst                                        Maintains data quality, dashboard and evaluation
Campaign lead                                  Turns weekly findings into execution decisions


Three checkpoints
       ●      Measurement gate: brief cannot be approved without baseline, target, source and owner.
       ●      Optimization gate: weekly performance must produce a documented decision.
       ●      Learning gate: campaign closure must add at least three findings to the shared benchmark & learning
              library.
These are the engine's gates. The Measurement gate is the Step-13 gate; the Learning gate feeds the Outcome
Library (M4). Measurement is built into the flow, not bolted on at the end.
pages.p-0101:
2. The personas
Each persona owns one failure mode. Together they cover the ways a reputation strategy dies.
 The Competitor “I can say that too.”
Catches: Table-stakes positioning; weak distinctiveness and ownability.
Attacks: Which of your claims could I make word-for-word? How do I counter-position you tomorrow? What's your
defensible ground versus mine? Is your “white space” actually contested?
Pass when: At least one position no named competitor can credibly claim, plus a stated defense against counter-
positioning.
 The CFO / Board “So what — where's the business and the number?”
Catches: No business linkage; vanity or vague measurement; unrealistic budget/timeline; over-claimed value.
Attacks: How does this move the business objective? What's the KPI, baseline, target and benchmark? Prove the
reputation-to-value link — or stop claiming it. Why fund this over the alternative?
Pass when: Every objective traces to a business goal; measurement has baseline/target/benchmark; value stated as
contribution, not attribution; budget realistic.
 The Journalist “Where's the substance? I'm going to check.”
Catches: Unsubstantiated claims; the gap between narrative and behaviour; greenwashing / hypocrisy exposure; spin.
Attacks: What's the proof behind this line? What does your actual record show? Where does the narrative outrun the
truth? What's the story when I dig?
Pass when: Every claim carries a proof point; no demonstrable gap between narrative and behaviour; no
greenwashing exposure (CSRD-safe).
 The General Counsel / Risk “Can you substantiate that — and what's the exposure?”
Catches: Legal/regulatory exposure; unsubstantiated or regulated claims; defamation; a stand that invites an
unwinnable fight; hidden tripwires.
Attacks: Is this claim substantiable and compliant? Does it create liability? Does the stand invite a fight we can't win?
Is there a litigation / disclosure / deal tripwire hiding here?
Pass when: Claims substantiable; do-not-say guardrails intact; no undisclosed tripwire; the stand fits the company's
risk appetite and character.
